# Installing Tidepool

Tidepool is a small job scheduler. This page covers every supported way of getting it onto a machine, from a single binary to a container image.

Back to the [documentation index](/index.md).

## Requirements

Tidepool needs very little to run. The scheduler itself is a static binary with no runtime dependencies, so the list below is about the machine and not about libraries.

- A 64-bit Linux, macOS or Windows host
- At least 128 MB of free memory
  - 512 MB if you enable the web console
  - 1 GB

- At least 128 MB of free memory
  - 512 MB if you enable the web console
  - 1 GB for clusters with more than fifty workers
- Network access to the workers on port 7400

Back to the [documentation index](/index.md).

## Install from a release

Download the archive for your platform and unpack it somewhere on your `PATH`:

```sh
curl -LO https://example.com/tidepool/v2.4.0/tidepool-linux-amd64.tar.gz
tar -xzf tidepool-linux-amd64.tar.gz
sudo mv tidepool /usr/local/

tar -xzf tidepool-linux-amd64.tar.gz
sudo mv tidepool /usr/local/bin/
tidepool --version
```

The last command should print `tidepool 2.4.0`. If it prints an older number, an earlier copy is shadowing the new one.

# Scheduling jobs

How the scheduler works
-----------------------

The scheduler keeps a queue of pending jobs ordered by priority and then by submission time. Every second it looks at the head of the queue and asks each idle worker whether it can take the job. A worker accepts when it has the labels the job requires and enough free slots. If no worker accepts, the job stays at the head and the scheduler tries again on the next tick. Jobs behind it are not considered until it has been placed, which keeps a large job from being starved by a stream of small ones. This strict ordering is simple to reason about but

job from being starved by a stream of small ones. This strict ordering is simple to reason about but it means one unplaceable job can hold up the queue. To guard against that, a job that has been at the head for longer than the stall timeout is moved to the parked list and an alert is raised. Parked jobs are retried every minute. Operators can also park and unpark jobs by hand, which is useful during maintenance windows. When a job is placed the scheduler records the decision in the audit log together with the worker it chose and the reason the other candidates were rejected.

Retries use exponential backoff.

Retries use exponential backoff. The first retry happens after two seconds, the second after four, and so on up to a ceiling of five minutes.

## Priorities

### Named levels

Jobs carry one of four named priority levels.

1. `critical` is reserved for system jobs.
2. `high` is for user-facing work.
3. `normal` is the default.
4. `low` is for batch work that can wait.

### Numeric priorities

A job may instead carry a number from 0 to 1000. Named levels map onto 900, 700, 500 and 100.

## Submitting a job

```yaml
# job.yaml
name: nightly-report
priority: normal
labels: [linux, gpu]
retries: 3
command: ["python", "report.py", "--date", "yesterday"]
env:
  REPORT_BUCKET: s3://reports
  LOG_LEVEL: info
timeout: 45m
```

Submit it with `tidepool submit job.yaml`. The command prints the job id.

# Command reference

## tidepool submit

Submit a job description to the scheduler.

| Flag         | Default  | Meaning                               |
|--------------|----------|---------------------------------------|
| `--wait`     | `false`  | Block until the job finishes          |
| `--priority` | `normal` | Override the priority in the file     |
| `--dry-run`  | `false`  | Validate the file without submitting  |

## tidepool park

Move a job to the parked list. Parked jobs are skipped by the scheduler until they are unparked or the retry timer fires.

## Minimal configuration

```yaml
listen: 0.0.0.0:7400
data_dir: /var/lib/tidepool
stall_timeout: 10m
workers:
  - name: alpha
    slots: 4
    labels: [linux]
  - name: beta
    slots: 8
    labels: [linux, gpu]
```

## Exit codes

- `0` success
- `1` the job failed
- `2` the job description was invalid
- `3` the scheduler could not be reached
